final_candidates.decision_summary: D172N exhibits high predicted antibody escape while achieving maximum ESM-1v sequence plausibility, indicating potent antigenic variation without compromising replication fitness.
R155K pairs a strong escape score with perfect PLM viability in the Sa/Sb antigenic region, providing a highly conservative substitution that reliably maintains viral fitness.
K157N delivers high antibody escape potential at a prominent antigenic loop site while maintaining favorable PLM plausibility and structural tolerability.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates have strong, corroborating phenotypic escape and replication viability signals, obviating the need for further evaluation.

history.rationale: Located in the Sa/Ca antigenic region of the HA head; aromatic substitution promotes antibody evasion while preserving local fold and receptor binding.
Moderate escape (0.781) with low plausibility (0.046) diminishes priority.
Shows modest MSA occurrence and escape potential, but ESM-1v score indicates impaired replication fitness.
Position 144 is a known antigenic site loop residue where polar variation can introduce steric hindrance to neutralizing antibodies without compromising HA stability.
Good escape prediction (0.823) but poor sequence plausibility (0.037) suggests compromised viral fitness.
Moderate MSA tolerance observed, but low ESM-1v score limits overall confidence compared to the top tier.
R155 resides in the Sa antigenic loop near the receptor binding margin; a conservative charge-conserving Lys substitution mediates immune escape while maintaining replication fitness.
Consistently excellent fitness profile (plm 1.000) combined with strong escape score (0.861) makes it an ideal candidate for viable escape.
High escape score paired with perfect ESM-1v score and strong MSA frequency (12.4%) confirms minimal replication cost. A premier conservative antigenicity-modifying substitution.
Position 157 in the Sa loop is directly targeted by neutralizing antibodies; Asn substitution diminishes antibody binding while preserving viral entry viability.
High antibody escape score (0.902) paired with reasonable sequence plausibility (0.407) supporting viability.
Exceptional antibody escape prediction with solid protein language model compatibility and natural MSA occurrence. Well tolerated at this key antigenic loop position.
A classic immune-escape position in H1 Sa antigenic site; S158N frequently alters epitope accessibility without disrupting head trimer architecture.
Decent escape potential (0.786) but modest sequence plausibility (0.185), slightly lowering confidence compared to top dual-performers.
Exhibits outstanding structural compatibility (z=0.928) on 1RUZ and high natural frequency in homologs (13.6%). Provides a dependable escape path via loop modification.
Surface-exposed loop residue in the Sb/Sa interface; Lys substitution alters antibody paratope recognition while maintaining electrostatic compatibility.
Moderate escape (0.758) accompanied by lower sequence plausibility (0.175), making it a secondary alternative.
Good structure compatibility and MSA tolerance confirm it maintains viral fold, though escape score is slightly lower than top candidates.
Charge-reversal at antigenic site Sb that strongly disrupts antibody interactions while being viable in circulating H1N1 strains.
Exceptional escape score (0.941) is heavily offset by near-zero sequence plausibility (0.004), raising strong viability concerns.
Despite high predicted escape, both structure compatibility (z=0.249) and ESM-1v indicate substantial fitness penalties.
Exposed residue in the 160-loop contributing to antibody neutralization epitopes; substitution to Asn removes positive charge and escapes recognition.
High escape potential (0.860) contradicted by low sequence plausibility (0.024).
Supported by structure compatibility and MSA presence, but low plm score keeps it below the top 4 candidates.
Position 172 forms part of the Sb antigenic site; Asp to Asn neutralizes negative charge, facilitating immune escape with high structural tolerance.
Shows both high antibody escape potential (0.881) and top-tier sequence plausibility (1.000), indicating strong replication fitness preservation.

Strong escape potential supported by ESM-1v plausibility and positive natural homolog presence. Structure evaluation was not applicable due to chain mapping mismatch but sequence priors strongly support viability.
Conserves aromatic/heterocyclic character at an exposed antigenic head position, reducing antibody binding affinity while sustaining folding fitness.
Poor performance on both escape (0.593) and sequence plausibility (0.004), placing it at the bottom.
Zero frequency in MSA, weak structure score, and poor ESM-1v support confirm it is unfavorable for replication.
